original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: An opt-in bounded-memory DAG serializer for the unchanged DisjointTensor.verify checks, with exact canonical-byte and complete-receipt equivalence and paired h=26 measurements.
scope_change_reason: Takes the explicit DAG-serialization question in Wentao Li PR2117. This is verifier engineering on a historical checker, not a new mathematical supplier or an audit of predecessor results.
bottleneck_link: Side result on review resources: avoid whole-document JSON allocation in a historical exact checker. This neither changes the binding complex supplier nor improves kappa.
stop_rule: Ship the first material allocation reduction with identical bytes and all checks. Stop after packaging; leave default adoption and compile-memory work open.
evidence: PROOF.md gives the scoped byte equivalence and buffer bound. verify.py checks 1623 schemas, six complete receipts through h=26, 41 rejecting controls and the complete nondigest checker AST. benchmark.py supplies five interleaved fresh-process pairs with exact receipt checks and separate traced-allocation runs.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.
